title: Stock market outlook today,25 Nov:Sensex, Nifty prediction-DJIA, S&P, NASDAQ, GIFT Nifty, Kospi, Nikkei, Taiwan cues | Stock Market News
text:
Stock market prediction for Wednesday, 25 November, 2026: The Indian stock market benchmark indices, Sensex and Nifty 50, are expected to have a gap-up today amid mixed global cues.

Asian markets opened lower, mirroring weakness on Wall Street, as a fresh sell-off in US technology shares reignited concerns about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence-led rally.

The MSCI Asia-Pacific Index fell 0.6%, giving back some gains after recording its biggest single-day advance since July on Tuesday. South Korea’s Kospi led the regional losses, sliding 3.7%.

Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, said Indian equity markets are likely to open sharply higher on Wednesday, with GIFT Nifty trading around the 25,700–25,750 range, pointing to a strong rebound following Monday’s steep sell-off. However, the ability to sustain the opening gains will remain key, particularly as persistent weakness across global markets continues to cloud sentiment and limit the scope for a decisive recovery.

Global cues remain cautious following Tuesday’s session on Wall Street. Weakness in technology stocks, particularly after Nvidia’s sharp reversal, continues to raise concerns over elevated AI valuations and the sustainability of the broader market rally.

Asian markets are trading sharply lower, with the Nikkei 225 down over 2% and the KOSPI down more than 5%, reflecting heightened risk aversion across the region. The divergence between GIFT Nifty and Asian markets suggests relative strength in domestic sentiment, although investors should remain cautious about potential selling pressure at higher levels.

On the commodities front, crude oil prices have recovered from their recent lows, with WTI trading in the $81–82 range, while precious metals remain under pressure.

The Sensex and Nifty 50 witnessed a sharp selloff, with the Sensex plunging nearly 1,484 points to record its steepest single-day fall in over four months. Heavy profit-booking across banking, financial and metal stocks erased gains from the previous two sessions, dragging the Nifty below the 25,350 mark.

The 30-share BSE Sensex declined 1,483.72 points, or 1.77%, to close at 82,435.99. Despite opening higher, the index quickly lost momentum and extended its losses to 1,523.83 points, or 1.81%, during the session, hitting an intraday low of 82,395.88.

The NSE Nifty 50 also ended sharply lower, shedding 450.95 points, or 1.75%, to settle at 25,349.65. This marked its biggest single-day decline since 8 July.

Hitesh Tailor, Technical Research Analyst at Choice Broking, said the Nifty 50 ended sharply lower at 25,349.65, falling 450.95 points, or 1.75%, as sustained selling pressure wiped out its initial gap-up gains. The index opened nearly 120 points higher at 25,929.15 and touched an intraday high of 25,992.60, close to the crucial 26,000 mark, before declining steadily to a low of 25,343.85.

He noted that the daily chart had formed a strong bearish engulfing candlestick pattern, indicating aggressive profit-booking and significant selling pressure near the 26,000 level. Sectoral performance was broadly weak, with the Metal index emerging as the biggest loser, declining 3.68%. PSU Bank, Bank, Financial Services and Energy stocks also witnessed heavy selling. IT was the top-performing sector, gaining 1.69%, while Realty showed some resilience.

On the technical front, Tailor placed immediate support for the Nifty 50 in the 25,000–25,100 zone, while resistance was seen at 25,500–25,600. The RSI had cooled to 66.34, slipping below its average of 75.59, signalling a sharp loss of short-term upward momentum.

Derivatives data also pointed to a cautious market setup, with the put-call ratio (PCR) declining to 0.74. The highest call open interest was concentrated in the 25,500–25,700 range, while the highest put open interest was seen between 25,300 and 25,000. Meanwhile, India VIX rose 2.18% to 17.6975. Tailor said the Nifty's ability to sustain above the 25,000–25,100 support zone would be crucial to preventing deeper corrective pressure.

The Gift Nifty Live Chart shows a weak start for the Indian stock market today. At 6:37 AM, the Gift Nifty was trading around the 25,765 level, a premium of 260.3 points from the Nifty futures’ previous close.

Sachin Gupta, VP – Technical Research at Choice Equity Broking Private Limited, said the Sensex closed at 82,435.99 on Monday, declining 1,483.72 points, or 1.77%. The index opened with a gap-up of around 502 points at 84,421.97 and initially touched an intraday high of 84,662.96 before witnessing sharp profit-booking. Selling pressure intensified after the index slipped below the 84,000 mark, eventually dragging it to an intraday low of 82,395.88, below 83,000.

He noted that the Sensex formed a bearish engulfing candlestick pattern on the daily chart after two consecutive sessions of gains, signalling a sharp reversal in sentiment and profit-booking following the recent rally. The breach of 84,000 and the subsequent close below 83,000 point to weakening near-term momentum.

Gupta placed immediate support for the index in the 81,700–82,150 range, with resistance at 82,900–83,200. He expects the Sensex to trade within the 81,700–83,200 range, with the near-term bias turning sideways amid continued profit-booking.

Nagaraj Shetti, Senior Technical Research Analyst at HDFC Securities, said the Nifty 50 witnessed sharp profit-booking on Monday after a strong rally over the past few weeks. The index slipped from highs near the 26,000 mark and ended the session with a steep 450-point loss.

He noted that the daily chart formed a long bearish candle after the market opened higher, completely engulfing the long bullish candle formed in the previous session on Friday. The price action points to a potential Bearish Dark Cloud Cover pattern, signalling a possible short-term reversal to the downside.
